item.title: A holomorphic motion with non-subharmonic Hausdorff dimension
item.description: arXiv:2610.22644v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present an example of a holomorphic motion of a Cantor set $\lambda \mapsto A_\lambda$ for which neither the Hausdorff dimension $\dimH(A_\lambda)$ nor the lower Minkowski dimension $\dimMl(A_\lambda)$ is a subharmonic function of~$\lambda$. This answers negatively a question of Fuhrer--Ransford--Younsi, and distinguishes these dimensions from packing and upper Minkowski dimensions, for which subharmonicity holds. All four dimensions are computed explicitly.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Ransford, Malik Younsi

item.title: Bounded Leaf Volumes and Analytic Quotients of Singular Holomorphic Foliations
item.description: arXiv:2610.22920v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a singular holomorphic foliation of dimension $k$ on a compact K\"ahler manifold $M$ of dimension $n$. Suppose that the volumes of its regular leaves are uniformly bounded, $\dim(Sing\mathcal{F})<k$, and the union of the leaf closures meeting $Sing\mathcal{F}$ has finite $2k$-dimensional Hausdorff measure. We prove that the quotient by chains of intersecting leaf closures is a normal compact complex analytic space of dimension $n-k$. The quotient map is proper and holomorphic, with connected fibers. The proof uses Bishop's theorems, Remmert and Stein extension, Barlet's cycle space, and Stein factorization. Away from the images of separatrices, the quotient has local charts given by finite holonomy groups. Examples show that these images need not coincide with the singular set of the quotient, and that bounded leaf volumes alone do not imply Hausdorffness. In codimension one, Malgrange's theorem makes the separatrix measure assumption automatic when $codim(Sing\mathcal{F})\geq 3$.
item.dc:creator: Carlos Eduardo Mart\'inez, Alberto Verjovsky

item.title: Approximation and extension theorems for normal affine toric varieties
item.description: arXiv:2610.22926v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study approximation and extension problems for holomorphic maps from Stein spaces to normal affine toric varieties, continuing the work of L\"ark\"ang and L\'arusson. Normality allows us to obtain twisted factorizations for arbitrary holomorphic maps from factorial complex spaces, including degenerate maps. This yields approximation and extension theorems under weaker cohomological assumptions. We also prove a simultaneous approximation and extension theorem under an additional codimension condition on the inverse image of the singular locus and a cohomological condition on the union of the interpolation submanifold and the approximation set. Finally, an explicit example with target $\{w^2=uv\}\cong\mathbb{C}^2/\{\pm1\}$ shows that simultaneous approximation and extension can fail even when the relevant cohomological obstructions vanish. Thus normality alone does not recover the full approximation and interpolation property of Oka manifolds.
item.dc:creator: Ryo Uchimoto

item.title: On extremal problems related to the Krzy\.{z} conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.23817v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study general extremal problems similar or closely related to the Krzy\.z conjecture and establish the structural properties of extremal functions, pointing out some differences with the original Krzy\.z case. We also introduce a family of more specific problems of this kind, interpolating between the Krzy\.z problem and the problem of maximizing the constant term, and show that they are closely related to the Krzy\.z conjecture: the conjecture implies the analogous statement for all of them and, conversely, if one of them has the same extremal value as the Krzy\.z problem, then this value is $2/e$. This may represent a new approach to attacking the original problem. Finally, we show that for these problems an extremal function whose Taylor coefficients $a_1,\ldots,a_{\lfloor n/3\rfloor}$ vanish must be the conjectured one; as a special case, we obtain a new proof of a recent result of MacDonald.
item.dc:creator: Sarah May Instanes, Adri\'an Llinares, Dragan Vukoti\'c

item.title: Brennan's Conjecture and the Universal Integral Means Spectrum
item.description: arXiv:2610.23853v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In October 2026, OpenAI released two preprints \cite{openai-brennan,openai-kraetzer}, establishing Brennan's celebrated conjecture~\cite{brennan,brennan2} and disproving Kraetzer's more general $t^2/4$ conjecture \cite{kraetzer, kraetzer-thesis}. While validating these results, we observed that much of their argument is redundant and arrived at a drastically shorter proof of a significantly stronger statement. The goal of this note is to give a short and concise presentation of the reborn proof, sacrificing some of the context and consequences for brevity, and relegating them to a follow-up work. In this particular case the human-AI interaction was fruitful and quite satisfactory, and hoping for a similar future in other subjects, we would paraphrase Rick Blaine: {\em ``AI, we hope this is the beginning of a beautiful friendship.''}
item.dc:creator: Ilia Binder, Oleg Ivrii, Istvan Prause, Stanislav Smirnov

item.title: Hausdorff Matrices on the BMOA and Bloch spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.22554v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We determine the spectrum and Fredholm essential spectrum of Hausdorff operators $\mathcal{H}_\mu$ on BMOA and the Bloch space $\mathscr{B}$, for suitable finite positive Borel measures $\mu$ on $(0,1]$.
item.dc:creator: Petros Galanopoulos, Alejandro Mahillo, Jesus Oliva-Maza, Aristomenis G. Siskakis

item.title: Cross-ratios and first order ordinary differential equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.22712v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate the usefulness of the cross-ratio in the study of first order odes of the form $y^\prime=P_ny^n+P_{n-1}y^{n-1}+\ldots+P_1y+P_0,\;\; (P_i)_{0\leqslant i\leqslant n}\in K,\;n\geqslant1$, where $K$ is a differential field of characteristic zero with algebraically closed field of constants. We discover along the way many differential algebraic identity between solutions to that equation. We also explain why the cross-ratio of any four solutions to such an equation is in general not constant when $n\geq3$ by exhibiting an obstruction which prevents its constancy when $n\geq3$. Finally to any separable polynomial $P_\varphi(z)=z^{n+1}+\varphi_1z^n+\varphi_2z^{n-1}+\ldots+\varphi_{n+1}$, $n\geq2$, over a differential field of meromorphic function on some domain of $\mathbb C$ with the usual derivation we associate a uniquely defined first order ode of the form $y^\prime=P_ny^n+P_{n-1}y^{n-1}+\ldots+P_1y+P_0,\;\; (P_i)_{0\leqslant i\leqslant n}\in K$ such that every root of $P_\varphi(z)$ is a solution to the said differential equation.
item.dc:creator: Oumar Wone

item.title: Nearly Sharp Uniform Projection Bounds and Superlinear Vitushkin Inequalities for Deterministic Self-Similar Sets
item.description: arXiv:2610.22908v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For each $\alpha\in(0,1)$, we construct an explicit deterministic finite homogeneous planar iterated function system of similarities satisfying the strong separation condition, whose attractor $E_\alpha$ has positive finite one-dimensional Hausdorff measure and, for all sufficiently small $\delta>0$, satisfies $\sup_{0\le\theta<\pi}H^1(\pi_\theta(N_\delta(E_\alpha)))\lesssim_\alpha(\log\delta^{-1})^{-\alpha}$. The defining system depends only on $\alpha$ and is fixed at every scale. For these same sets, we prove the sharp analytic capacity law $\gamma(N_\delta(E_\alpha))\asymp_\alpha(\log\delta^{-1})^{-1/2}$ as $\delta\rightarrow0$. Consequently, each $E_\alpha$ satisfies the quantitative Vitushkin comparison $\operatorname{Fav}(N_\delta(E_\alpha))\lesssim_\alpha\gamma(N_\delta(E_\alpha))^{2\alpha}$ for every $\delta\in(0,1)$. These comparisons are superlinear for $\alpha>1/2$, with exponents arbitrarily close to the optimal upper limit two for this class of self-similar sets. A completely specified sixteen-map system gives $\alpha=53/100$ and comparison exponent $53/50$. Inspired by Falconer's Venetian blind constructions, the projection argument combines exact collinear cylinder subfamilies, quantitative distribution of word orientations, and a cover indexed by first successful symbolic blocks. The rotation parameters are explicit powers of a real algebraic number, linking the construction to simultaneous Diophantine approximation. The capacity estimate follows from the curvature characterization of analytic capacity and a telescoping inequality for cylinder masses.
item.dc:creator: Caleb Marshall

item.title: Spectral Schwarz Lemmas and Parallel Obstructions to Metric Comparison
item.description: arXiv:2610.23011v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we characterize when comparison of contracted Chern curvatures implies comparison of Hermitian bundle metrics with the same constant on compact Hermitian bases. If the curvature contraction of the reference metric is semipositive, this implication holds for every Hermitian metric if and only if the kernel of this contraction contains no nonzero subbundle parallel with respect to the Chern connection of the reference metric. The equality terms of a $C^2$ spectral truncation identify the parallel summand on which comparison can fail, without regularity assumptions on the curvature kernel. We also establish a sharp operator estimate, with a constant independent of the bundle ranks, for holomorphic bundle maps on complete K\"ahler bases under curvature bounds and bounded base-map energy density. Smooth Schatten moments give global control without a separate boundedness assumption on the bundle map. Finally, we obtain rank bounds and conditions for vanishing on compact Hermitian bases from directional curvature traces over fiber subspaces. For higher-dimensional subspaces, these conditions allow mixed signs on individual fiber lines.
item.dc:creator: Xu Pang, Yao Sha, Ren Xin-An

item.title: Seven ordered points and the nonexistence of arithmetic ball quotient compactifications
item.description: arXiv:2610.23227v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that the ordered GIT quotient of seven points on $\mathbb P^1$ with equal weights is not isomorphic to the Baily--Borel compactification of any arithmetic complex ball quotient. Together with our companion paper and the known positive examples, this determines the equal weight case for every $n\ge6$: such a realization exists precisely for $n=6,8$. The lattice and the algebraic isomorphism are unrestricted, and torsion and divisorial ramification are allowed. The proof combines arithmetic reductions with identities involving Chern classes of fixed subvarieties and intersection inequalities for nef divisors on the GIT quotient. The final comparison includes all fixed components and requires no bound on the degree of an individual fixed curve.
item.dc:creator: Ryunosuke Nakano (Hokkaido University), Hisato Matsukawa (Hokkaido University)

item.title: Weighted configurations and the nonexistence of arithmetic ball quotient compactifications
item.description: arXiv:2610.23228v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that, for every $n\ge9$, no ordered GIT quotient of $n$ points on $\mathbb P^1$ with positive rational weights smaller than one and of total weight two is isomorphic to the Baily--Borel compactification of an arithmetic complex ball quotient. The weights may lie on stability walls, and the lattice may have torsion and ramify along divisors. No compatibility with a prescribed period map is assumed. The proof compares homomorphisms from the tangent bundle to line bundles of negative degree with normal bundles of arithmetic fixed subvarieties. We describe these homomorphisms through coincident marked points and prove vanishing statements for their kernels. The comparison, together with integrality of Chern classes and the invariant theory of finite reflection groups, gives the nonexistence theorem without a Fano assumption on the GIT quotient.
item.dc:creator: Ryunosuke Nakano (Hokkaido University), Hisato Matsukawa (Hokkaido University)

item.title: Complete harmonic metrics and subharmonic functions on the complex plane
item.description: arXiv:2610.23441v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper continues our previous work \cite{Miy6} on an extension of the Li--Mochizuki theorem concerning the existence and uniqueness of complete diagonal harmonic metrics on cyclic Higgs bundles over open Riemann surfaces. We consider the extended Hitchin equation associated with general subharmonic weight functions on the canonical bundle, not necessarily induced by holomorphic $r$-differentials. We establish uniqueness of complete solutions with determinant $1$ for arbitrary subharmonic weight functions, without additional regularity assumptions on them. We also prove that, on the complex plane, such a complete solution exists whenever the weight function is not identically $-\infty$. Furthermore, if $(\varphi_\epsilon)_{\epsilon>0}$ is a family of smooth subharmonic weight functions decreasing to such a weight function $\varphi$ as $\epsilon\searrow0$, the associated family of smooth complete solutions $(h_\epsilon)_{\epsilon>0}$ with $\det(h_\epsilon)=1$ converges monotonically to the unique complete solution $h$ associated with $\varphi$ and satisfying $\det(h)=1$.
item.dc:creator: Natsuo Miyatake

item.title: Higher-order sum rules for zeros of the planar Gaussian entire function
item.description: arXiv:2610.23697v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish marginal sum rules for the truncated correlation functions of zeros of the planar Gaussian entire function (GEF). For each fixed integer $k\ge2$, the integral in one coordinate converges absolutely and equals $-(k-1)$ times the truncated correlation of order $k-1$. This answers the marginal-identity question posed by Krishnapur and Yogeshwaran for the planar GEF. We also prove a criterion for simple point processes under local moment and absolute integrability assumptions. Suppose there is a sequence of compactly supported cutoffs between zero and one that are eventually equal to one on each compact set. If the variances of their linear statistics tend to zero, the marginal identities hold almost everywhere. Strong clustering and variance bounds for smooth linear statistics verify these assumptions for GEF zeros. The proof uses mixed cumulants and the partition formula relating ordinary and factorial cumulants.
item.dc:creator: Xiaolin Zhu, Feng Guo

item.title: Modulus of elementary domains in the hyperbolic plane
item.description: arXiv:2512.00358v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the modulus of curve families inside elementary domains in the hyperbolic plane $\bH^1_\C$. We establish exact expressions for the modulus of connecting and separating curve families in a hyperbolic circular annulus. For the symmetric hyperbolic quadrilateral $Q(a,b)$, we obtain lower bounds by restricting the curve families to particular foliations, and upper bounds by constructing admissible densities. These estimates bracket the modulus. We also present numerical evidence showing how close the bounds are, how they behave asymptotically, and we evaluate them for specific values of $(a,b)$.
item.dc:creator: Ioannis D. Platis

item.title: The Schwarzian Derivative for Convex Holomorphic Mappings in Several Complex Variables
item.description: arXiv:2604.12010v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We obtain upper bounds for the norm of the Schwarzian derivative of convex holomorphic mappings defined on the polydisk and the unit ball in $\mathbb{C}^n$. For coordinate-wise convex mappings on the polydisk, we derive a sharp estimate extending the classical one-variable result of Chuaqui--Duren--Osgood to higher dimensions. For the Roper--Suffridge extension operator in the unit ball, we obtain an explicit bound that represents the best available estimate in this setting.
item.dc:creator: Rodrigo Hern\'andez

item.title: Examples of Uniformly Quasiregular Mappings with Fatou Set Having Infinitely Many Components
item.description: arXiv:2606.27746v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct examples of uniformly quasiregular mappings (uqr) acting on a sphere and having Fatou set consisting of infinitely many components. In particular we construct a uqr mapping providing a higher dimensional counterpart for the polynomial $z \mapsto z^2 - 1$ acting on the extended complex plane $\hat{\mathbb{C}}$.
item.dc:creator: Gaven Martin, Kirsi Peltonen

item.title: A Database of Continued Fractions of Polynomial Type
item.description: arXiv:2409.06086v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We describe a database of 1925 continued fractions with polynomial coefficients, of which more than 1600 are new, both for interesting constants and for transcendental functions, and provide the database inside the \TeX\ source of the paper. Look in particular at the section ``Table of Contents''.
item.dc:creator: Henri Cohen

item.title: Shannon entropy for harmonic metrics on cyclic Higgs bundles
item.description: arXiv:2410.08571v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $X$ be a Riemann surface, $K_X$ its canonical bundle, and $T_X=K_X^{-1}$. A diagonal harmonic metric $h=(h_1,\dots,h_r)$ on a cyclic Higgs bundle of rank $r\geq 2$ associated with a holomorphic $r$-differential $q$ induces Hermitian metrics $H_j=h_j^{-1}\otimes h_{j+1}$ on $T_X$ for $j=1,\dots,r-1$, together with a possibly degenerate metric $H_r$ determined by $h_1,h_r$, and $q$. This construction depends on $q$ only through the subharmonic weight $\phi_q=\frac{1}{r}\log|q|^2$ on $K_X$. In previous work, we extended harmonic metrics to solutions associated with arbitrary subharmonic weight functions $\varphi$, yielding analogous metrics $H_1,\dots,H_r$. For each nonzero real parameter $\beta$, we introduce a function on $X$, which we call entropy, that quantifies their mutual misalignment. By extending estimates of Dai--Li and Li--Mochizuki to general subharmonic weight functions, we obtain upper and lower bounds for $\beta>0$ when $H_1,\dots,H_{r-1}$ are complete and the weight is neither induced by a complete flat K\"ahler metric nor identically $-\infty$. The upper bound is $\log r$, the constant entropy associated with a complete flat K\"ahler metric, for which $H_1=\cdots=H_r$. The lower bound is the constant entropy associated with the weight $\varphi\equiv-\infty$. Furthermore, for every nonzero real $\beta$, we determine the asymptotic behavior, as $r\to\infty$, of the difference between these two entropy values, showing that it converges to a finite real number if and only if $\beta>-1$.
item.dc:creator: Natsuo Miyatake

item.title: Complete harmonic metrics and subharmonic functions on the unit disc
item.description: arXiv:2508.12848v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $X$ be a Riemann surface with canonical bundle $K_X$ and holomorphic tangent bundle $T_X=K_X^{-1}$. For each integer $r\geq 2$, each $q\in H^0(K_X^r)$, and each choice of a square root of $K_X$, we obtain a cyclic Higgs bundle. A diagonal harmonic metric $h=(h_1,\ldots,h_r)$ induces Hermitian metrics $H_j=h_j^{-1}\otimes h_{j+1}$ on $T_X$ for $j=1,\ldots,r-1$, together with a possibly degenerate Hermitian metric $H_r$ determined by $h_1,h_r$, and $q$. We call $h$ complete if the K\"ahler metrics induced by $H_1,\ldots,H_{r-1}$ are all complete. Li--Mochizuki proved that if $q$ is nonzero unless $X$ is hyperbolic, there exists a unique complete harmonic metric on the corresponding cyclic Higgs bundle satisfying $\det(h)=1$. The Hitchin equation depends on $q$ only through the subharmonic weight $\phi_q=\frac{1}{r}\log|q|^2$ on $K_X$. We establish uniqueness of complete solutions with determinant $1$ for general subharmonic weight functions $\varphi$ whose exponentials are $C^2$ outside a compact subset of $X$. On the unit disc $\mathbb D=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|<1\}$, we also prove that a real complete solution exists for every subharmonic weight function. We further establish a monotone approximation theorem. If $\varphi_\epsilon$ are smooth subharmonic weight functions on the discs $\mathbb D_\epsilon=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|<1-\epsilon\}$ decreasing to $\varphi$ as $\epsilon\searrow0$, the corresponding complete solutions $h_\epsilon$, normalized by $\det(h_\epsilon)=1$, converge monotonically to a complete solution $h$ associated with $\varphi$.
item.dc:creator: Natsuo Miyatake

item.title: L\"{o}wner equations and de Branges--Rovnyak spaces
item.description: arXiv:2512.10368v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study one-parameter families of de Branges--Rovnyak spaces associated with the radial and chordal L\"{o}wner equations. Our approach is based on a classical but little-known technique of the de Branges school. In this paper, we recast this technique in the theory of direct integrals and integral operators. As an application, we prove Fourier-type expansion theorems induced by the L\"{o}wner equations, and give answers to a problem posed by Fricain--Hartmann--Ross.
item.dc:creator: Michio Seto

item.title: Hyperbolicity and fundamental groups of complex quasi-projective varieties (III): applications
item.description: arXiv:2512.20360v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper is Part III of a series of three. We begin by introducing the notion of $h$-special varieties, which can be seen as varieties "chain-connected by the Zariski closures of entire curves." We prove that if $X$ is either a special smooth complex quasi-projective variety in the sense of Campana or an $h$-special variety, then for any linear representation $\rho:\pi_1(X)\to {\rm GL}_N(\mathbb{C})$, the image $\rho(\pi_1(X))$ is virtually nilpotent. We also provide examples showing that this result is sharp, leading to a revised form of Campana's abelianity conjecture for smooth quasi-projective varieties. In addition, we prove a structure theorem for quasi-projective varieties with big and semisimple representations of the fundamental groups, thereby addressing a conjecture by Koll\'ar in 1995. We also construct several examples of quasi-projective varieties that are special and $h$-special, highlighting certain atypical properties of the non-compact case in contrast with the projective setting.
item.dc:creator: Benoit Cadorel, Ya Deng, Katsutoshi Yamanoi

item.title: Complex Hyperbolic Immersions of Cheng--Yau Metrics on Thullen Domains
item.description: arXiv:2608.21911v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We classify the homotheties of the complete Cheng--Yau K\"ahler--Einstein metrics on the two-dimensional Thullen domains $M(\mu)$, $\mu>0$, that admit K\"ahler immersions into $\mathbb{CH}^{\infty}$. With $\Ric(g_{\mathrm{CY}})=-3g_{\mathrm{CY}}$, an immersion of $c\,g_{\mathrm{CY}}$ exists exactly when $0<\mu\leq\mu_+$ and $0<c\leq3\min\{1,\mu\}/(\mu+2)$. The critical parameter $\mu_+>1$ is characterized by an explicit equation, and its endpoint is included. Every admissible metric has a proper global K\"ahler embedding. The same parameter interval classifies immersibility into flat and projective Hilbert space, where every positive homothety admits a proper global embedding. Beyond the wall, all three targets are excluded at every positive scale. The proof combines an algebraic normalization of the Cheng--Yau equation, all-order coefficient estimates, and complex continuation of a scalar flow. For $\mu\neq1$, the resulting complete nonhomogeneous examples disprove proposed K\"ahler--Einstein rigidity conjectures in the complex-hyperbolic and flat Hilbert settings. We also prove a complementary rigidity theorem for Bergman--Hartogs domains and construct complete $\eta$-Einstein Sasakian manifolds with nonhomogeneous Riemannian metrics and proper global Sasakian embeddings into the infinite-dimensional Heisenberg space form.
item.dc:creator: Mirel Caib\u{a}r, Andrea Loi
